dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Hi, yes, hello. I'm calling about water running out of a pipe at the curb on my street. It's been going for days and it's not even raining. There hasn't been a storm, nothing.
Okay, a pipe at the curb, water coming out. Whereabouts is this?

225 Van Zandt Avenue, in the North End. The pipe comes out of the curb, right in front of my house, and the water just keeps coming. Every night it freezes. Now the whole sidewalk is a sheet of ice. Mō, abunai, it's dangerous, sorry. Dangerous. Somebody is going to fall.
No, you're fine. Van Zandt, two twenty-five, water from a pipe at the curb, icing over the sidewalk. Got it. Is there a lot of water, or more of a trickle?

It's not a trickle. It runs down along the gutter and pools at the low spot by the corner. When the car goes by it throws it. The depth, it's about up to the hubcaps in the worst part. I measured it against my neighbor's car.
Up to the hubcaps, wow. [pause] Sorry, I'm hearing some kind of thumping on your end, is that you?
Oh, that's, I'm standing outside, there's a truck idling down the block. Like a pulsing, like an engine far away. Can you still hear me okay?
Yep, I can hear you fine, it's just a low hum. So how long has this been going on, would you say?

Almost two weeks now. First it was small, I thought, okay, maybe a pipe from somebody's sump pump. But it keeps getting bigger. And I already told, um, nobody. I didn't call before, but I'm telling you, it's two weeks and nothing is fixed. Somebody should have noticed. They drive by here every day.

Understood. I'm writing this down: Van Zandt Avenue, constant dry-weather flow from a curb pipe, freezing on the sidewalk, ponding at the corner. Now, you said it's a pipe at the curb. Is it a round pipe sticking out of the curb face, or is it coming up through the street?
Out of the curb. Round, about this big, maybe six inches. Metal, I think. The water is clear, not dirty. It doesn't smell.
Can I ask something? Is it a city drain, or a state one? Because somebody told me Van Zandt is, how do you say, kenmichi, the state road. Sorry. I don't know whose it is.

No worries. Van Zandt is a busy road, so that's a fair question. Honestly, part of it can be state-owned. I'd have to check the map for your block. Either way, I'll log it here and get it in front of our drainage folks, and if it turns out to be the state's, we'll pass it along to them ourselves. You don't have to chase that.
Okay. But I don't want it to be passed and passed. That's what happens. Everybody says not my department.
I hear you. I'll put it down as a safety issue because of the ice, that bumps it up. Can I get a name and a number in case they need to reach you?
Yuki Patel. Four-oh-one, five five five, zero one nine five.
Yuki Patel, four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-five. Is that a cell?
Yes, cell. I'm outside now, so if the signal [line breaks up] drops, call again.
Will do. In the meantime, if you've got sand or ice melt, put some down in front of your place. It won't stop the water but it'll help people walking by.
I did already, one bag. It just freezes again by the morning. It's the same every day. I am tired of it, honestly. Two weeks.
Yeah, that's a long time for that. I'll flag it today. Someone from the drainage side should get out to look, probably in the next day or two, and they'll call you if they need more.
A day or two. Okay. If nobody comes I will call again, I'm telling you now.
That's fine, call anytime and mention Van Zandt and the ice. I've got it noted with my name on it.
Okay. Thank you, Kevin. Arigatō, sorry, thank you.
No problem at all. Take care out there, and watch your footing.
